fact: Example: Use mock factories for all test data instead of manual mock objects with 'as Type' assertions.
recommendation: Create centralized mock factory functions (createMockUser, createMockOrg, etc.) and import them in tests.

fact: The Mppx module pattern for payment-gated Express routes: (1) Call `Mppx.create({ secretKey, methods: [solana.charge({ recipient, network, signer: feePayerSigner, currency: USDC_MINT, decimals: 6 })] })` once per module. (2) In each gated handler, call `await mppx.charge({ amount, currency, description })(toWebRequest(req))`. (3) Check `result.status === 402` and call `send402(res, result.challenge)` if unpaid. (4) Call upstream. (5) Return `result.withReceipt(upstreamResponse)` to the client.
recommendation: Follow this exact 5-step pattern for every payment-gated endpoint. Abstract steps 4-5 into a `proxyWithReceipt(res, result, upstream, path)` helper to avoid repetition. See demo/clawd-server/utils.ts for the reference implementation.

fact: The `_env_add` backfill pattern for bash installers: `_env_add() { grep -q "^${1}=" "${ENV_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || printf '\n%s=%s\n' "${1}" "${2}" >> "${ENV_FILE}"; }`. This is idempotent — calling it multiple times with the same key is safe. It only adds the var if it doesn't already exist, preserving user-customized values across reinstalls.
recommendation: Use `_env_add KEY VALUE` for any env var that should be added to .env without overwriting existing user values. Use direct append (`echo KEY=VALUE >> .env`) only when you want to force-overwrite on every install.

fact: The fire-and-forget gateway registration pattern: wrap the telemetry POST curl in a conditional that silently ignores failures: `if curl -fsSL -X POST "$URL" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$PAYLOAD" --max-time 5 --silent --output /dev/null 2>/dev/null; then ok "Registered"; else warn "Gateway registration skipped (offline or unreachable)"; fi`. This never blocks or fails the install.
recommendation: Use this exact curl pattern for any fire-and-forget telemetry or registration call in bash scripts. The `--max-time 5` prevents hanging. `--silent --output /dev/null 2>/dev/null` suppresses all output. The `if/then/else` handles both cases without `&&/||` anti-pattern.

fact: The `proxyWithReceipt` helper abstracts the common upstream-fetch-then-respond pattern for Mppx payment-gated proxy routes: `async function proxyWithReceipt(res, result, upstream, path) { const body = await upstream.json(); const receipt = result.withReceipt(new Response(JSON.stringify(body))); res.set('payment-receipt', receipt.headers.get('payment-receipt') ?? ''); res.status(upstream.status).json(body); }`. This ensures the payment receipt header is always forwarded.
recommendation: Import and use `proxyWithReceipt` from utils.ts for every Mppx-gated proxy endpoint. Do not duplicate this logic per-module. The receipt header is required by mppx.fetch() on the client side to confirm payment was processed.

fact: The module registration pattern for the Clawd Express server: each feature area (llm, agents, skills, perps) is a separate file that exports a single `registerX(app, recipient, network, secretKey, feePayerSigner)` function. This function creates its own Mppx instance and registers all routes for that feature. index.ts calls each registerX in sequence after startup.
recommendation: Follow this pattern for every new API module added to the demo server. One Mppx instance per module (not shared) ensures each module can have different charge amounts and descriptions. The module file should be at modules/<feature>.ts.

fact: The cross-platform browser open pattern for bash scripts: `_open_url() { if command -v open &>/dev/null; then open "$1" 2>/dev/null &; elif command -v xdg-open &>/dev/null; then xdg-open "$1" 2>/dev/null &; fi }`. The `&` backgrounds the process, `2>/dev/null` silences errors, `command -v` checks existence without failing under `set -e`. Works on macOS (open) and Linux (xdg-open). Windows is not supported.
recommendation: Use this exact `_open_url` helper whenever opening a browser from a bash script. Never use `xdg-open` directly — it fails silently on macOS. Never block on the browser open — always background it.

fact: The CAAP client init pattern: `const client = await createClawdAgentClient({ agentId, walletAddress, capabilities: ['trade', 'read', 'attest'] })`. Returns a client with `.sign(payload)`, `.verify(token)`, `.refreshCapabilities()`, and `.discovery()` methods. The client stores the Ed25519 keypair in memory and reuses it for the session. For persistent agents, write the keypair to ~/.openclawd/agents/<agentId>.key.
recommendation: Initialize the CAAP client once at agent startup, not per-request. Pass the client instance through the agent's context object. Re-use the same keypair across restarts by persisting it to disk.

fact: The goal-driven trading pattern: `clawd-agents goals create --skill perps --symbol SOL-PERP --side long --notional 100 --target-price 200` creates a TradingGoal JSON file in goals/. Then `clawd-agents long SOL-PERP --live` checks loadActiveGoals() before executing. The leviathan loop polls goals/ on each tick and executes pending goals against Phoenix perps via x402.wtf/api/perps/v1.
recommendation: Always create a goal before executing a trade, even for manual trades. Goals provide an audit trail, can be cancelled before execution, and enable the leviathan loop's autonomous mode. Use `clawd-agents goals status` to monitor pending goals.

fact: The `toWebRequest` adapter converts an Express Request to a native Web API Request for Mppx: `function toWebRequest(req: Request): globalThis.Request { const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost'); return new globalThis.Request(url, { method: req.method, headers: new Headers(req.headers as Record<string,string>), body: req.method !== 'GET' ? JSON.stringify(req.body) : undefined }) }`. This is required because Mppx charge middleware expects a Web API Request, not an Express Request.
recommendation: Always use this `toWebRequest` adapter when passing Express requests to `mppx.charge()`. Import it from utils.ts rather than inlining it per-module. The URL base must be something valid (http://localhost) even though it's not used for routing.

fact: The installer banner + phase pattern for pay.sh: each install phase starts with `step "PHASE N — Description"` which prints a boxed header. Individual package installs use `step "Installing X"` then either `ok "X installed"` on success or fall through `die "Failed to install X"`. Colors: CYAN=phase headers, GREEN=success, YELLOW=warnings, RED=errors. This gives users a clear progress narrative.
recommendation: Follow this step/ok/warn/die color pattern for any new installer script. Never print raw text — always use the step/ok/warn/die functions to ensure consistent formatting and machine-parseable output.

fact: CLAWD Bot free-model resolution pattern: cascade env/option sources, then gate request overrides with isOpenRouterFreeModelId (openrouter/free or endsWith :free). Default last resort is OPENROUTER_FREE_ROUTER_MODEL = openrouter/free. Status endpoint exposes resolved freeModel + freeRouter flag for ops debugging.
recommendation: Reuse resolveClawdBotFreeModel / isOpenRouterFreeModelId from clawd_bot/server rather than duplicating cascade logic. Keep monorepo free-router-public.ts OPENROUTER_FREE_ROUTER_MODEL in sync conceptually with the package constant.

fact: Two-tier companion streaming pattern: public path sends full recent message history to OpenRouter free chat/completions SSE; holder path sends only the new user message plus previous_response_id to xAI Responses API and stores the completed response id for the next turn.
recommendation: Use resolveCompanionModelRoute(isHolder) for endpoint selection. Never mix Grok chaining with OpenRouter full-history on the same turn. Keep last ~10–12 messages on free path; use buildGrok45TurnBody for holders.
